ei.title: 처벌보다 인내: 아이는 가벼운 결과를 여러 번 겪으며 스스로 배운다

fullPassage: Many of the parents we work with say things like, “I’ve tried everything. I’ve grounded him, taken away his Xbox, turned off the Internet, and made him quit the soccer team. I’ve got nothing left to take away.” When a kid repeatedly misbehaves, the temptation is to think, Well, they’ll never learn with a five-foot wall. Better make it ten feet. But Ross Greene, who is also a champion of collaborative problem-solving, points out that the kids who get the most negative consequences often learn the least from them. Years of research have shown that children can become self-disciplined, empathic, compassionate, and successful adults without painful punishment. So if they don’t seem to learn after a mild consequence, give them time. They might have to crash into that five-foot wall more than you’d like them to. Be patient. Express confidence that they’ll figure it out. They will.

questions.passage: Many of the parents we work with say things like, “I’ve tried everything. I’ve grounded him, taken away his Xbox, turned off the Internet, and made him (A)[____ / join] the soccer team. I’ve got nothing left to take away.” When a kid repeatedly (B)[misbehaves / behaves], the temptation is to think, Well, they’ll never learn with a five-foot wall. Better make it ten feet. But Ross Greene, who is also a champion of collaborative problem-solving, points out that the kids who get the most negative consequences often learn the least from them. Years of research have shown that children can become self-disciplined, empathic, compassionate, and successful adults without painful punishment. So if they don’t seem to learn after a mild consequence, give them time. They might have to crash into that five-foot wall more than you’d like them to. Be (C)[patient / angry]. Express confidence that they’ll figure it out. They will.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ quit — misbehaves — patient: 부모는 아이가 축구팀을 '그만두게' 했고(처벌 목록), 아이가 반복해서 '잘못 행동할' 때 벽을 높이고 싶어지며, 결론은 '인내심을 가지라'는 것
❌ ① join(가입시키다)은 빼앗는 처벌 목록의 흐름과 모순
❌ ② behaves(바르게 행동하다)라면 벽을 높이고 싶은 유혹이 생길 이유가 없음
❌ ④ angry(화난)는 기다리고 믿어 주라는 결론과 반대

But Ross Greene, who is also a champion of collaborative problem-solving, points out that the kids who get the most negative consequences often learn the least from them. Years of research have shown that children can become self-disciplined, empathic, compassionate, and successful adults without painful punishment. So if they don’t seem to learn after a (A)[____ / severe] consequence, give them (B)[money / time]. They might have to crash into that five-foot wall more than you’d like them to. Be patient. Express (C)[doubt / confidence] that they’ll figure it out. They will.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ mild — time — confidence: 연구가 처벌 없이도 성장한다고 했으므로 '가벼운' 결과 뒤에는 '시간'을 주고, 해낼 것이라는 '자신감'을 표현하라는 흐름
❌ ① severe(가혹한)는 시간을 주고 기다리라는 온건한 조언과 모순
❌ ② money(돈)는 문맥과 무관
❌ ③ doubt(의심)는 아이가 해낼 것이라는 신뢰 표현과 반대

But Ross Greene, who is also a champion of collaborative problem-solving, points out that the kids who get the most negative consequences often learn the (A)[____ / most] from them. Years of research have shown that children can become self-disciplined, empathic, compassionate, and successful adults without (B)[pleasant / painful] punishment. So if they don’t seem to learn after a mild consequence, give them time. They might have to (C)[lean / crash] into that five-foot wall more than you’d like them to. Be patient. Express confidence that they’ll figure it out. They will.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① least — painful — crash: 부정적 결과를 가장 많이 받는 아이가 가장 '적게' 배우고, '고통스러운' 처벌 없이도 성장하며, 5피트 벽에 '부딪히며' 스스로 배운다는 비유
❌ ② most(가장 많이)는 Ross Greene의 지적(처벌이 많을수록 덜 배운다)과 반대
❌ ③ pleasant(즐거운)는 punishment(처벌)와 의미상 모순
❌ ④ lean(기대다)은 실패를 몸으로 겪는다는 crash의 비유와 부적합
det.tip: learn the least: 가장 적게 배우다 (최상급)

questions.passage: Many of the parents we work with say things like, “I’ve tried everything. I’ve got nothing left to take away.” When a kid repeatedly ②<u>misbehaves</u>, the temptation is to think, Well, they’ll never learn with a five-foot wall. Better make it ten feet. But Ross Greene, who is also a champion of collaborative problem-solving, points out that the kids who get the most ③<u>negative</u> consequences often learn the least from them. Years of research have shown that children can become self-disciplined, empathic, compassionate, and ④<u>miserable</u> adults without painful punishment. So if they don’t seem to learn after a mild consequence, give them time. They might have to crash into that five-foot wall more than you’d like them to. Be patient. Express confidence that they’ll figure it out. They will.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① grounded: 외출 금지시켰다 — 처벌 목록으로 적절
✅ ② misbehaves: 잘못 행동하다 — 적절
✅ ③ negative: 부정적인 결과 — 적절
❌ ④ miserable: self-disciplined, empathic, compassionate 등 긍정적 자질 나열 끝에 '비참한' 어른은 모순. 원문은 successful(성공적인)

So if they don’t seem to learn after a mild consequence, give them time. They might have to crash into that five-foot wall more than you’d like them to. Be ④<u>patient</u>. Express confidence that they’ll figure it out. They will.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① repeatedly: 반복적으로 잘못 행동하다 — 적절
❌ ② opponent: Ross Greene은 협력적 문제 해결을 지지하는 인물로, 처벌의 비효율을 지적하는 문맥. '반대자'는 모순이며 원문은 champion(옹호자)
✅ ③ self-disciplined: 자기 절제력 있는 — 긍정적 성장 목록으로 적절
✅ ④ patient: 인내심을 가지라는 결론 — 적절

But Ross Greene, who is also a champion of collaborative problem-solving, points out that the kids who get the most negative consequences often learn the ②<u>most</u> from them. Years of research have shown that children can become self-disciplined, empathic, compassionate, and successful adults without painful punishment. So if they don’t seem to learn after a ③<u>mild</u> consequence, give them time. They might have to crash into that five-foot wall more than you’d like them to. Be patient. Express ④<u>confidence</u> that they’ll figure it out. They will.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① temptation: 벽을 높이고 싶은 '유혹' — 적절
❌ ② most: Ross Greene의 지적은 부정적 결과를 가장 많이 받는 아이들이 가장 '적게'(least) 배운다는 것. '가장 많이' 배운다면 처벌 반대 논리가 성립하지 않음
✅ ③ mild: 가벼운 결과 — 적절
✅ ④ confidence: 해낼 것이라는 자신감 — 적절
det.tip: the least(가장 적게) ↔ the most(가장 많이)

det.analysis: ✅ confidence: 타동사 Express의 목적어 자리이므로 명사가 필요. confident(형용사: 자신 있는) → confidence(명사: 자신감). 뒤의 that절은 confidence와 동격

questions.passage: Many of the parents we work with say things like, “I’ve tried everything. I’ve grounded him, taken away his Xbox, turned off the Internet, and made him quit the soccer team. I’ve got nothing left to take away.” When a kid repeatedly misbehaves, the temptation is to think, Well, they’ll never learn with a five-foot wall. Better make it ten feet. But Ross Greene, who is also a champion of collaborative problem-solving, points out that the kids who get the most negative consequences often learn the least from them. Years of research have shown that children can become self-disciplined, empathic, compassionate, and successful adults without painful punishment. So if they don’t seem to learn after a mild consequence, __________. They might have to crash into that five-foot wall more than you’d like them to. Be patient. Express confidence that they’ll figure it out. They will.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② give them time(그들에게 시간을 주어라): 처벌 없이도 배운다는 연구 뒤에, 가벼운 결과로 못 배우면 '시간을 주라'는 조언. 뒤의 Be patient(인내하라)와 자연스럽게 연결
❌ ① take away more of their things(더 많은 것을 빼앗아라)는 글이 비판하는 처벌 강화
❌ ③ make the wall ten feet high(벽을 10피트로 높여라)는 글이 경계하는 유혹
❌ ④ stop expressing confidence(자신감 표현을 멈춰라)는 뒤의 조언과 정반대

ch: take away more of their things
make the wall ten feet high

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: often learn the least from them(종종 그것들로부터 가장 적게 배운다)
det.analysis:
✅ ① often learn the least from them: Ross Greene의 지적 = 부정적 결과를 가장 많이 받는 아이들이 종종 가장 '적게' 배운다. 뒤의 '처벌 없이도 성장한다'는 연구와 논리적으로 연결
❌ ② always learn the most from them(항상 가장 많이 배운다)은 처벌 옹호 논리로 글과 반대
❌ ③ are eager to solve problems together(함께 문제 해결에 열심이다)는 벌 받는 아이의 학습량 논의와 무관
❌ ④ never crash into the same wall again(같은 벽에 다시 부딪히지 않는다)은 여러 번 부딪히며 배운다는 후반 내용과 모순
det.tip: the most(가장 많이) ↔ the least(가장 적게)
